# the contributor audit: all-point triangle pairing and critical variance embedding

## Triangle pairing: PASS

I read `candidate 4ffd81a5b3e6f9fb`
in full and ran the standard-library verifier. Its 6380 exact shift
minimizations and 1573 stationary-branch checks pass.

The ordinary area formula `4BC` treats one-vertex and two-vertex cuts,
including vertex boundaries. The intercepts `2B,2C` are feasible since
the second-largest barycentric coordinate is at most one half. In the
paired calculation the piecewise quadratic tail is continuously
differentiable at both support endpoints and at its interior knot;
therefore the regime classification does not omit transition minima.
The proper straddling stationary shift is feasible exactly on the
displayed interval. Its further reduction is a concavity argument in
the vertex-height parameter, not a same-normal Jensen assertion.

At the limiting repeated-height endpoint, the bound
`lambda_i(1-lambda_i)>=C(1-C)>=2BC` is valid for each vertex label.
Dominated convergence is justified by the nonzero limiting height
range and null line boundaries. Boundary candidate points have zero
ordinary and paired depth by a supporting cap. The example with
nonzero shift is consistent with the theorem and shows why a stronger
fixed-normal inequality would be false. No higher-dimensional or
mixed-fiber conclusion is inferred.

## Actual critical variance and binary embedding: PASS

I read `candidate 8ac7846221e4d65a`
in full. The star fibers `K,K-K,-K` have strict midpoint compatibility,
and their central symmetry proves the exact critical mass `D=M/2`.
Each specified cap divides the middle fiber in half and has complementary
endpoint traces, so all cap budgets really equal that same attained
critical value. With the other fibers fixed the cap constraints differ
from the one-simplex constraints by constants; the stationary Hessian
therefore transfers exactly. Only that block is claimed stationary.

For the binary embedding, fixing an integer binary coordinate forces
every constituent of a convex combination to have that same coordinate.
This proves both the complete integer support and the exact fibers,
without replacing their union by its convex hull in the measure.
The explicit regular-base functional loses at least three on a different
binary component and gains at most two in the remaining coordinate.
It therefore supplies the asserted strictly positive isolation gap.
Bounded fiber supports give finite cap tilts with strict exclusions.

The isolated cap cover supplies the global upper bound `D`. The old
star center and regular simplex centroids supply matching lower bounds
from actual subsets, so the maximum is exactly `D`. The mass formula
and ratio `2^n/(2^n-2+2Gamma_d)` follow by direct summation.

The redundant group count is material and is correctly stated:
`2^n+d-1` groups are displayed, and one star group would suffice for
coverage. Thus the example does not refute a statement about a chosen
minimal cover with at most `2^n` groups or about all normal stresses.
Nor does it certify stationarity under variations of all fibers and
cap parameters. It disproves only the specified local critical-variance
exclusion, including a proposed dimension-d-only relative gap criterion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
